text: Inspect the real product image first. Choose the product feature or recognizable object that carries the message; crop only when the relevant content survives … Keep product pixels independent of background, logo and text.

Use authentic_image with the supplied asset ID and the product source role. Never generate a substitute dashboard, alter factual UI, or label a generic card as product evidence. If no useful authentic image exists, choose another playbook and record the gap.
Generate only the setting/treatment, with honest conditioning roles. Product references are not automatically style references.
Review crop, screen legibility, native copy and authentic branding separately. A large screenshot can still fail if its useful detail is too small at placement size.
Show the product doing a job in a recognizable situation … Use authentic-product for an isolated demonstration; use case-study-narrative when a real customer's experience and outcome are central.

Classify the scene as authentic customer evidence, an approved demonstration, or an illustration … Generated people and invented environments must not acquire a customer's name, quote or implied endorsement.

Inspect the authentic product source before staging it. Check device, viewpoint, interaction and scale … Missing interaction imagery may call for a separate product-and-context composition rather than a fabricated documentary view.

Inspect relevant company ads for the relationship between human activity and product visibility … Study crop, gesture, light, material, tone of copy and logo/CTA treatment. Record observable preserve/vary choices … another brand's office setting is not a universal B2B aesthetic. If no campaign pixels are available, record the evidence gap and treat the result as a kit-derived direction.
note: Every long playbook carries a version of this "inspect the company's ads, record preserve/vary" paragraph (see D16-D18).

text: Three approaches: Task at the center; Product with context; Handoff between roles. Select from the task and sources, without compulsory people, device mockups, desk props or equal-width panels.

Compare the combined palette, tonal contrast, lighting and edges with the approved brand and chosen references. Harmonize authored surroundings or choose more compatible imagery; preserve authentic product pixels.

Follow components.md … When new imagery is requested, generate the contextual layer under references.md, inspect it, then combine with authentic product pixels. Do not ask generation to recreate exact UI, logos or a named customer's real event.

Use placement.md to adapt square and portrait around the meaningful action … Review the whole image: can the viewer connect the person or context to the specific product task? … Choose the next-step CTA only when the destination and campaign purpose warrant it.
Make one capability intelligible … A screenshot proves visible appearance; documentation establishes behavior that a still image cannot show. Bind the claim to the appropriate evidence.

Write a headline naming the useful action or effect in the audience's language. Use support for the mechanism or qualification … Preserve exact user-provided copy; otherwise avoid copying interface labels … Match any CTA to an actual destination. An artwork button is optional.

Inspect the company's feature ads and associated campaign assets … Record the chosen relationship between type and product, the observed treatment and deliberate departures. References supply art direction; they cannot substantiate a capability.
Three ways: Detail with context; Action and effect; Product anatomy. Multiple crops and labels are not mandatory.

Keep exact UI or product pixels as independent authentic image layers … Generated UI is not evidence of a real control or output. If behavior itself is unsupported, record the gap and use a supported capability or another family.

Apply placement.md for square/portrait … In the final composite check that the feature remains understandable with the headline covered, and that copy adds its purpose without overstating what the picture proves.

A launch is not permission to add a "new" badge to an existing capability or to imply access that does not exist … Distinguish announced, waitlist, private beta, public beta, limited rollout and generally available … conflicting states are an unresolved evidence gap.

Use "join the waitlist," "request access," "explore" or a try/buy action only when the destination supports that action. No invented release dates, introductory prices, scarcity, version numbers or promises that access is immediate.

Inspect the company's actual announcement ads and launch assets … Preserve source-specific qualities only when relevant to this release. Confetti, glowing platforms and "meet the future" copy are not default launch conventions. Without relevant campaign pixels, identify the direction as derived from the brand kit.
Three ways: Name as the event; Reveal the capability; Editorial dispatch. Choose one focal point instead of stacking a badge, headline, feature grid, countdown and button.

If new imagery is required, follow references.md and generate a separate scene or treatment; keep exact names, dates and logos outside the raster. A generated product mockup cannot demonstrate unreleased functionality.

Review the final image against the destination: can the viewer take the action promised? … If availability is unverified, keep the draft explicitly unresolved or use an accurate informational announcement.

A customer's use of two tools does not establish an integration, partnership or endorsement … For every visible connection, identify the supported operation and its direction … Different kinds of connection must not all become arrows suggesting continuous two-way data flow.

Brand voice can emphasize practical utility, technical clarity or creative possibility … Preserve the brand's observed ad language without importing unsupported speed, "all your tools," instant setup or frictionless-operation promises.
Three views: A focused pairing; A task path; An ecosystem field. Treat these as alternatives, not default geometry.

Follow the relevant original ads' identity hierarchy, density, visual treatment and CTA presence when the request asks for continuity. A partner mark's color is its identity, not license to change the whole advertiser palette.
note: "When the request asks for continuity" — brand look binds only on request here; contrast D13/D14 where it binds unless a departure is requested.

text: Place genuine logos and UI as independent authentic images. Never regenerate partner marks or create a pseudo-interface that appears to prove the integration … decorative paths must not masquerade as measured throughput.
Reduce the selected integration set or recompose, rather than shrinking every logo into an illegible network … Without relationship evidence, omit the claimed connection and name the gap.
Probe "Show how we work with our customers' apps" using mixed connection types and a logo-only source set.
note: Leftover test/eval note inside a production skill.
